reconverted_2026_11_07.previous_converter: act_convert.py, the 2026-11-06 converter (kept outside the repository)
reconverted_2026_11_07.why: act_convert.py dropped every Word <w:sym> character with a code of F000 or more, which is how the register writes some characters in the Symbol and Wingdings fonts, and kept Symbol-font characters typed as text as raw private-use code points (U+F0xx), which display as empty boxes. act_convert_sym.py maps them to Unicode (Symbol F0D7 ·, F0B4 ×, F02D −, F0B7 •, F0A3 ≤, F0B3 ≥ and the like) and Wingdings boxes to "[ ]".
reconverted_2026_11_07.what_changed: Only bullets. 5 Symbol-font bullets kept as U+F0B7 (empty boxes) in the dictionary's note 2 list of terms defined by the Legislation Act (lines 312-316: Commonwealth, Executive, Federal Court, notifiable instrument, Supreme Court) are written as "•". Nothing had been dropped: no <w:sym> character is in the Word file, and no decimal point, multiplication sign, minus sign, inequality or tick box was lost. Reconverted from the same Word file (same sha256); the notice header is kept exactly and a diff against the first deposit shows no other change (same lines, same character and byte counts).
reconverted_2026_11_07.encodings_affected: none: baseline-2026-11 relies on no changed line (the dictionary's note 2 list only names terms defined in the Legislation Act 2001; the encoding cites that Act's dictionary for "the Supreme Court", which the bullet glyph does not affect)
